observation: The supremum ranges over S_\tau although only \mathcal{S}_\tau was defined at line 986.

observation: The base-change bound uses f(\beta + 1) although no bare \beta is fixed in this paragraph.

observation: The second site axiom is tested in Cov_{\kappa,f(\alpha)} and the cofinal bound concludes \beta < \beta_1.

observation: The proof defines W_{a,i} but the final coproduct uses W_{i,a}.

observation: The graph proof chooses j and j' in E although the vertex set is denoted V and no set E is defined.

observation: The set A is defined as a set of closed subsets, but the displayed partial order is written on alpha and alpha' through undefined objects Z_alpha and Z_alpha'.

observation: The limit lemma writes J as a subset of plain I, although the indexing category is denoted by calligraphic I and no plain set I is defined.

observation: Two formulas use X setminus U union V without parentheses in a proof that requires the complement of the union.

observation: The asserted strictly decreasing chain contains X setminus U_i1 union U_i2 without parentheses.

observation: The displayed definition of U_K has an unmatched extra closing parenthesis after the set-builder expression.

observation: The finite-union identity is written E = bigcup E intersect V_j without a union index or grouping.

observation: The chain omits the subset sign before Z_e and calls Z_0 through Z_e irreducible closed subsets of X although they lie in Y.

observation: For Y contained in Y' and their generic points xi and xi', the direction of specialization and the sign of the dimension difference appear reversed.

observation: After reduction to a Noetherian space the text says a finite union of irreducible components is not necessarily closed.
adverse_evidence: Irreducible components are closed and a finite union of them is closed; the intended warning is plausibly that the union is not necessarily open.

observation: The proof asserts that T = X minus E is nowhere dense immediately from density of E, before deriving that conclusion from the locally closed pieces.

observation: The product-spectral proof establishes irreducibility of p(Z) and q(Z) but then chooses generic points of the closures of p(X) and q(Y).

observation: A map is defined as f : X to product_U W but the next sentence calls it f : X to Y before Y is defined as f(X).

observation: With f : V to U and g : W to V the text says to lift g composed with f.

observation: The pseudo-functor data are written alpha_{f,g} although the defining lemma writes alpha_{g,f}.

observation: The inertia category is written I_mathcal{S} in one formula although the object is otherwise mathcal{I}_mathcal{S}.

observation: After constructing a functorial isomorphism from d to c composed with b, the concluding sentence calls it d to b composed with c.

observation: The terminal expression contains a duplicated composition operator: (a tensor b) composed composed 1^{-1}.

observation: The tensor functor of a symmetric monoidal category is declared on mathcal{C} tensor mathcal{C}.

observation: The product of slice categories is identified with mathcal{C}/U times V.

observation: After defining Z'_i as constructible-topology subspaces the proof writes Z' = lim Z_i.

observation: The proof invokes quasi-compactness of the spectral topology on Z while citing the constructible-Hausdorff-quasi-compact lemma.

observation: The conclusion writes W minus E = lim U_i minus E without parentheses.

observation: The canonical map X to X^* is said to identify X with an open subspace of X.

observation: The Rainwater proof defines E = X minus U intersect f^{-1}(V) without parentheses and immediately calls E closed and identifies its complement with U intersect f^{-1}(V).

observation: The proof starts with X' = beta(Y), extracts a minimal closed E contained in X', and proves E extremally disconnected, but the uniqueness paragraph reverts to a map g : X' to X'' and invokes minimality of X'.
adverse_evidence: Only E has been proved minimal; beta(Y)=X' need not be. The uniqueness argument is valid after replacing or renaming X' by E.

observation: A lemma contains the literal list item 'add more here.' and its proof is only 'Omitted.'.

observation: The definition says one partition refines another when the parts of the first are unions of parts of the second, reversing the standard refinement relation used by the following example.

observation: The normal-core argument chooses right-coset representatives G = union H g_i but intersects g_i H g_i^{-1}.

observation: The colimit proof declares a functor I to Top but immediately says its values are topological groups G_i and constructs a representability functor on TopGroup.

observation: Descending-chain condition is said to produce a smallest member of A.

observation: The finite union X = Z union Z_1 union ... Z_n omits the final union operator.

observation: The intersection V_{j_0,k} intersect V_{j_1} ... intersect V_{j_p} omits the intersection operator after V_{j_1}.

observation: Noetherian DCC is again said to produce a smallest member of S.

observation: The basis refinement sets J = {i_x | x in U} and V_j = B_{i_x}, which is not well-defined if different x choose the same i_x but different basis elements.

observation: The quotient-map complement identity reverses X and Y and takes E as a subset of the wrong space.

observation: After choosing alpha' and alpha'' the proof suddenly uses an unchosen alpha with Z_alpha = Z_alpha' intersect Z_alpha''.

observation: The refinement operation is asserted to decrease N by exactly one and therefore to be repeated exactly N times.
adverse_evidence: It eliminates the selected bad tuple and can eliminate others simultaneously; the preceding factorization shows no new bad tuple appears, so only a decrease by at least one is justified.
proposed_smallest_correction: Say N decreases by at least one and the procedure terminates after at most the original N repetitions.

observation: The inverse-limit proof embeds Gamma_phi times the product over l not equal to j,k in the full product, which is ill-typed when phi is an endomorphism and j = k.

observation: The lemma promises a 'third point' specializing to x and y without assuming x and y distinct.
adverse_evidence: The common specializing point produced by the proof may equal x or y, for example when one specializes to the other.
proposed_smallest_correction: Remove 'third' and say 'a point specializing to both x and y'.

observation: An equivalence list ends with the literal unfinished item 'add more here.' while the proof treats only the preceding conditions.

observation: The sentence f(gw) = t for all w in W leaves g unquantified.

observation: The proof says a point y 'corresponds to a point of' a nonempty open intersection rather than using density from hypothesis (c).

observation: The proof says E intersect Y contains an open V but omits that V is nonempty.

observation: The statement requires a directed union of closed subsets but the proof exhibits only the family of point closures and does not show it is directed.

observation: The expressions U minus U intersect closure(B) and U minus U intersect closure(A) are unparenthesized and parse ambiguously.

observation: Both vertical arrows in the naturality square are labelled rho^U_V, although one is the restriction of F and the other that of G.

observation: The data declare 0 as an element of A, but the next sentence calls both zero and negation 'maps'.

observation: The proof says 'the presheaf of continuous function is a sheaf'.
adverse_evidence: The referenced example and the construction concern the presheaf of all continuous functions; the singular count noun is ungrammatical.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace 'continuous function' by 'continuous functions'.

observation: The sentence begins 'Lemma ... show that'.

observation: The clause says 'psi ... is morphism of presheaves'.

observation: The parenthesis reads 'into the restriction of G to a O-module'.

observation: The hypothesis says 'Let F be a sheaf O-modules'.

observation: The plural subject 'the restriction mappings' is followed by singular 'is'.

observation: The definition of a presheaf with values in a category imposes composition compatibility but does not require rho^U_U to be the identity.

observation: The definition of a morphism gives a single phi:F(U) to G(U) without quantifying U; it also says 'with value' rather than 'with values'.

observation: The phrase reads 'defines the structure of an O(U)-module structure'.

observation: The phrase 'For U subset X open set' is missing a determiner or copula.

observation: The phrase says 'the set of morphism of sheaves'.

observation: After defining F only as a presheaf and correctly referring to its underlying presheaf at lines 1112-1113, line 1127 calls it the 'underlying sheaf of sets'.

observation: The Yoneda sentence says the adjunction formula determines the pullback 'uniquely'.

observation: The canonical map G(U) to f_pG(f^{-1}(U)) uses U without introducing it as an open subset of Y.

observation: The sentence reads 'let U subset X open'.

observation: The proof says 'restruction map'.

observation: Two hypotheses say 'an g-map'.

observation: The second of two announced assignments uses G to f_pG rather than G mapsto f_pG.

observation: The sentence has two successive predicates: 'the corresponding map ... is the map ... is also a map'.

observation: For f:X to Y the paragraph puts F on Y and f_*F on X.

observation: A comma separates the compound subject 'the pullback and pushforward functors' from singular 'is'.

observation: A display ending with a full stop is followed by the lowercase fragment 'according to Section ...'.

observation: The hypotheses and Hom categories are for presheaves, but the third equality is called an equality 'of abelian sheaves'.

observation: A display ending with a full stop is followed by lowercase 'where'; 'Lemmas' is plural before one reference.

observation: A display ending with a full stop is followed by lowercase fragment 'which are a combination of'.

observation: The definition says 'Denote i_x ... the inclusion map'.

observation: The lemma says `there exist an idempotent $e\in R$`.

observation: After defining $\Delta=\operatorname{Res}_x(g,h)$ and localizing at $\Delta$, the proof says `$\operatorname{Res}_x(f,g)$ is invertible`.

observation: In the case $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=(0)$, the classification says $\mathfrak p$ must be generated by nonconstant polynomials and concludes it is generated by one irreducible polynomial.

observation: After applying the Euclidean algorithm in $k(x)[y]$ and clearing denominators, the proof states `$p=af+bg$ for $p,a,b\in k[x]$`.

observation: Gauss's lemma is used to choose $a,b\in k(x)$ with `$ah\mid f$ and $bh\mid g$ for $ah,bh\in k[x]$`.

observation: After defining $f(z)=A(z)g(z)+a$ and assuming $\deg(g)<2$, the proof writes `$h(z)=c_1z+c_0$`.

observation: The higher-degree expansion ends `$f(z)=A(z)^2h(z)+b_1B(z)+b_0A(z)$`.

observation: The sentence introduces `for a ring T` with the mathematical symbol $T$ outside math mode.

observation: The second covering generator changes from `$(z^2+z+2a-2)(z-a)$` at lines 5043–5045 to `$(z^2+z+2a-a)(z-a)$` at line 5049.

observation: The ring $\mathbf Q[z,1/(z-a)]$ is called the localization of $\mathbf Q[z]$ `at the maximal ideal $(z-a)$`.

observation: After writing $R=\prod R_i$, the proof says this induces similar product decompositions for both `$R$ and $S$`.

observation: The lemma says `There exists elements $r_i\in R$`.

observation: The sentence contains the duplicated construction `an element ... such that ... such that`.

observation: The text declares `$g'\in S'$` and then writes `$g'\notin\mathfrak q$`, although $\mathfrak q$ is an ideal of $S$.

observation: The lemma begins `Let $R$ be Noetherian local`.

observation: The dimension lemma says `Any maximal chain of ideals` has length $d$.

observation: For a module of depth $e$, the lemma always displays a complex beginning with `$F_{d-e-1}$`.

observation: After proving that the fibre point $\overline{\mathfrak q}'$ is closed, the proof says this follows from `$\mathfrak q'$ being closed`.

observation: Two enumerated conclusions read `$R'\to B$ not quasi-finite at any prime ...`.

observation: The proof says `there are finitely may primes`.

observation: With the fibre at a fixed prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, the proof calls $\mathfrak q_i$ primes of $S$ `lying over $R$`.
adverse_evidence: A prime of $S$ lies over a prime ideal of the base, not over the ring as an object; the preceding line fixes the fibre at $\mathfrak p$ and the residue-field extensions in the next lines are over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

observation: The proof defines $I_d$ by the leading term $ax^d$ `for each integer $d$`.
adverse_evidence: Negative exponents do not belong to the formal power-series ring $R[[x]]$; the subsequent ascending chain begins at $I_0$ and all later ranges use $d=0,\ldots,d_0$.

observation: After displaying an equality for the element $f$, the proof says it `is contained in $I'$`.
adverse_evidence: Containment is a relation between subsets; the displayed $f$ is an element and belongs to the ideal $I'$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `is contained in` by `belongs to` (or `lies in`).

observation: The proof says `$\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian ring`.
adverse_evidence: The singular predicate noun requires an indefinite article.

observation: The proof says `Chains of primes ideals`.

observation: The lemma says `there exists an $t\in\mathfrak m_R$`.
adverse_evidence: The symbol name is pronounced with an initial consonant sound and takes the article `a`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `an $t$` by `a $t$`.

observation: The conclusion calls the quotient map `an isomorphsm`.

observation: The sentence reads `the derivative of $f$ is invertible in $T$ in particular is not contained in $\mathfrak q$`.
adverse_evidence: Two finite predicates are run together without a conjunction or punctuation; invertibility supplies the stated nonmembership consequence.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `is invertible in $T$ and in particular does not belong to $\mathfrak q$`.

observation: A period is placed inside the displayed factorization after `$S'_{\mathfrak m'}$`, and the next line begins the fragment `of the ring map ...`.
adverse_evidence: The pre-display clause `there is a factorization` is completed by the post-display prepositional phrase; the intervening period wrongly splits one sentence into a complete clause and an orphaned fragment.
proposed_smallest_correction: Remove the period after the displayed target and end the sentence after `of the ring map $R\to S'_{\mathfrak m'}$`, or recast the lead-in so the display closes the sentence.

observation: The lemma says a unit `is a $n$th power`.
adverse_evidence: The ordinal symbol is pronounced with an initial vowel sound and requires the article `an`; the next clause in the same sentence uses `an $n$th power` correctly.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `a $n$th power` by `an $n$th power`.

observation: In a single equality of vector-space dimensions, the third term is written `\dim(\overline{\mathfrak m}/\overline{\mathfrak m}^2)` while the first two terms explicitly use `\dim_\kappa`.
adverse_evidence: Here `\overline{\mathfrak m}/\overline{\mathfrak m}^2` is a vector space over the same residue field `\kappa=R/\mathfrak m`; an unqualified dimension is ambiguous and breaks the displayed equality's explicit scalar-field binding.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the third `\dim` by `\dim_\kappa`.

observation: The proof cites Lemma `lemma-regular-graded` for the statement that each regular local ring $R_i$ is a domain.
adverse_evidence: Lemma `lemma-regular-domain` immediately states `Any regular local ring is a domain`; `lemma-regular-graded` instead identifies the associated graded ring and is only an ingredient in the proof of that direct result.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `lemma-regular-graded` by `lemma-regular-domain`.

observation: The coordinated list `1, x, ..., x^{d-1}` is followed by the singular verb `is a B'-basis`.
adverse_evidence: The displayed basis has multiple elements and takes plural agreement.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `is a $B'$-basis` by `are a $B'$-basis`.

observation: After differentiating `T^p-1=\prod_{j=0}^{p-1}(T-\alpha_j)` at $T=\alpha_i$, the displayed product starts with $(\alpha_i-\alpha_1)$ and also ends with $(\alpha_i-\alpha_1)$.
adverse_evidence: The derivative is the product over every $j\ne i$ with $0\le j\le p-1$; the printed formula duplicates the $j=1$ factor and omits the boundary factors $j=0$ and $j=p-1$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the endpoints by `(\alpha_i-\alpha_0)` and `(\alpha_i-\alpha_{p-1})`, retaining the omitted $j=i$ factor under the hat.

observation: The proof resumes after a display with the editorial residue `OK, and the elements ...`.
adverse_evidence: `OK` has no mathematical or grammatical role in the published proof and reads as an unremoved drafting marker.
proposed_smallest_correction: Delete `OK, ` and begin the sentence `The elements ...`.

observation: The coordinated gerund subjects `taking tensor products and taking integral closures` are followed by the singular verb `commutes`.
adverse_evidence: Two coordinated operations form a plural grammatical subject.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `commutes` by `commute`.

observation: The proof says the element `$f/1 \in S^{-1}R$ is contained in every prime ideal`.
adverse_evidence: Containment is a relation between subsets; an element belongs to or lies in an ideal.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `is contained in` by `belongs to` (or `lies in`).

observation: A lemma whose only algebra variable is $S$ concludes by discussing `R \to R \otimes_k R` and `\dim_k(R)`.
adverse_evidence: $R$ is undefined in this lemma and proof; the direct argument concerns the stated $k$-algebra $S$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace all three occurrences of $R$ in the final direct-argument clause by $S$.

observation: The proof reads `Writing $k_i=(a_{i,j})_{j\in J}$ and we obtain what we want`.
adverse_evidence: The initial participial clause cannot be coordinated with the finite predicate by `and` in this construction.
proposed_smallest_correction: Delete `and`: `Writing ..., we obtain what we want.`

observation: For an arbitrary ring map $\varphi:R\to S$, the proof says `\sum_{i\ne0}a_{i,j}s_i\in R`.
adverse_evidence: The sum is an element of $S$, and $R$ has not been identified with a subring because $\varphi$ need not be injective. The lemma's condition (2b) correctly requires membership in $\varphi(R)$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `\in R` by `\in \varphi(R)`.

observation: The displayed matrix factorization and all subsequent products use uppercase matrices $Y$ and $Z$, but their defining sentence says `let $y$ be the row vector ... and let $z$ be the column vector`.
adverse_evidence: Lowercase $y,z$ are not used as matrices afterward; the sentence is intended to define the uppercase $Y,Z$ appearing in $(g)=YXZ$, $YX$, and $XZ$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace lowercase `$y$` and `$z$` in the vector-definition sentence by `$Y$` and `$Z$`.

observation: The universal differential is printed as `g \mapsto \frac{\partial g}{\partial x_i}\mathrm{d}x_i\otimes1` with a free index $i$.
adverse_evidence: Immediately above, the variation formula sums over every $i$, and the differential of a polynomial is `\sum_i (\partial g/\partial x_i)\mathrm{d}x_i`; without the sum the displayed map is not defined independently of an unbound index.
proposed_smallest_correction: Insert `\sum_i` before the partial-derivative term.

observation: With $B=P/J$, $B'=P/J'$, and $J'=(f_i)+J^2\subset J$, the proof says the differentials generate modulo the nilpotent ideal `$J'/J^2$`.
adverse_evidence: The nilpotent kernel ideal of the surjection $B'=P/J'\to B=P/J$ is $J/J'$. By contrast, $J'/J^2$ is not an ideal of $B'$ and cannot be the modulus used for Nakayama in the stated module.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace both occurrences of `$J'/J^2$` in this sentence by `$J/J'$`.

observation: After tensoring $0\to J\to R\to R/J\to0$ with $R/I$, the printed cokernel is `$R/I + J$`.
adverse_evidence: The tensor product $(R/J)\otimes_R(R/I)$ is the quotient ring $R/(I+J)$; the printed unparenthesized expression is neither that quotient nor the correct cokernel of the displayed map.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `$R/I + J$` by `$R/(I + J)$`.

observation: The sentence reads `then $x\in I$ implies ..., implies $x$ maps to zero ...`.
adverse_evidence: The repeated finite verb `implies` produces an ungrammatical chain; the second step is the consequence of the first implication.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the second `implies` by `and hence` (or split the sentence equivalently).

observation: For (2)⇒(1), the proof cites `lemma-pure-ideal-determined-by-zero-set` after showing supports of quotients by pure ideals are open.
adverse_evidence: That lemma proves only uniqueness of a pure ideal from its vanishing set. The required existence for every closed subset stable under generalizations is the bijection in `lemma-pure-open-closed-specializations`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the citation `lemma-pure-ideal-determined-by-zero-set` by `lemma-pure-open-closed-specializations`.

observation: For ring maps $R\to S\to S'$, the kernel $J'$ is defined using the multiplication map `$S'\otimes_{R'}S'\to S'$` although $R'$ is nowhere defined.
adverse_evidence: The displayed comparison, the proof, and the concluding differentials all use the common base ring $R$; $J'$ must be the diagonal ideal in $S'\otimes_R S'$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the undefined subscript `$R'$` by `$R$`.

observation: For an $S$-module $M$ and ring map $S\to S'$, the lemma sets `$M'=S'\otimes_R M$`.
adverse_evidence: The asserted base-change identity begins with $S'\otimes_S P^k_{S/R}(M)$ and the extension has codomain $S'\otimes_S N$; the intended extended $S'$-module is therefore $S'\otimes_S M$, not restriction followed by tensor over $R$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `$S'\otimes_R M$` by `$S'\otimes_S M$` in the definition of $M'$.

observation: The principal-parts equality chain prints `S'\otimes_R S'/(J')^{k+1}` twice and `S'\otimes_R M'/(J')^{k+1}(S'\otimes_R M')` without grouping the tensor-product numerators.
adverse_evidence: $J'$ is an ideal of $S'\otimes_R S'$, not of the final $S'$ factor, and its induced action is on $S'\otimes_R M'$; the preceding lemma states the correctly grouped quotient explicitly.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write `((S'\otimes_R S')/(J')^{k+1})` at both occurrences and `(S'\otimes_R M')/(J')^{k+1}(S'\otimes_R M')` at the module occurrence.

observation: The final object in the principal-parts chain is `$P^k_{S'/R'}(M')$`, but the lemma defines only $R\to S\to S'$.
adverse_evidence: The statement and all preceding terms concern differential operators relative to $R$, and the immediately preceding lemma concludes with $\Omega_{S'/R}$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the undefined base `$R'$` by `$R$`.

observation: The extension paragraph takes the codomain and both scalar extensions of $\gamma$ over $R$, writing `$S'\otimes_R N$` and `$S'\otimes_R P^k_{S/R}(M)$`.
adverse_evidence: Here $M,N,$ and $P^k_{S/R}(M)$ are $S$-modules and the lemma statement requires the extension $M'=S'\otimes_S M\to S'\otimes_S N$ along $S\to S'$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace each of the three displayed/inline `\otimes_R` subscripts in the extension construction by `\otimes_S`.

observation: The lemma statement ends `such that the universal differential operators of order $k$ to the map given by ...`, with no finite verb and a plural noun for the single universal operator.
adverse_evidence: The isomorphism identifies the universal differential operator with the displayed map; the present wording is grammatically incomplete and suppresses that identification.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `such that the universal differential operator of order $k$ corresponds to the map given by ...`.

observation: The proof says `choose a closed point $t$ of space $T\cap D(f)$`.
adverse_evidence: The noun `space` refers to the specific topological space just constructed and requires the definite article.
proposed_smallest_correction: Insert `the`: `of the space $T\cap D(f)$`.

observation: The proof says a nonzero element `$x\in R$ is contained in at most finitely many maximal ideals`.
adverse_evidence: An element belongs to an ideal rather than being contained in it; `at most finitely many` is redundant and obscures the intended finiteness assertion immediately restated as `$V(x)$ is finite`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `belongs to only finitely many maximal ideals` (or `lies in only finitely many maximal ideals`).

observation: The cardinality assertion ends with a period and is followed by the fragment `Because the cardinality of $I\times\ldots\times I$ is ...`.
adverse_evidence: The `Because` clause supplies the reason for the preceding cardinality bound and has no independent main clause.
proposed_smallest_correction: Join the clauses with `, because` or begin `This is because ...`.

observation: The lemma says `there exist a commutative diagram`.
adverse_evidence: The existential verb agrees with the singular noun phrase `a commutative diagram`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `exist` by `exists`.

observation: The proof defines $P_d=\ker(F_{d-1}\to F_{d-2})$ only `at least if $d\ge2$`, then uses that formula to claim the displayed finite-projective resolution for every $d\ge0$.
adverse_evidence: For $d=1$ the relevant projective module is $\ker(F_0\to M)$, and for $d=0$ it is $M$ itself, exactly as separated in conditions (3) and (4) of the cited preceding lemma. The printed proof leaves both boundary cases unhandled and invokes undefined negative-index modules if read literally.
proposed_smallest_correction: Add the two boundary cases explicitly: for $d=1$ take $P_1=\ker(F_0\to M)$; for $d=0$ use that $M$ is already finite projective. Then retain the displayed construction for $d\ge2$.

observation: The section introduction says `an G-unramified ring map`.
adverse_evidence: The letter name `G` begins with a consonant sound and takes the article `a`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `an G-unramified` by `a G-unramified`.

observation: The third parallel criterion says `of finite type (resp. presentation)` while the two immediately preceding criteria say `of finite type (resp. finite presentation)`.
adverse_evidence: The parenthetical alternative is the standard property `finite presentation`; omitting `finite` breaks the parallel terminology and yields the nonstandard phrase `of presentation`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Insert `finite`: `of finite type (resp. finite presentation)`.

observation: Item (1) reads `we have $\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ is the maximal ideal`.
adverse_evidence: The sentence runs the predicates `we have` and `is` together; the equality identifies an ideal, which the following clause characterizes.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `$\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$, which is the maximal ideal ...`.

observation: The coordinated subject `the characterization ... and the structure ...` is followed by the singular verb `shows`.
adverse_evidence: Two cited results jointly supply the implication and form a plural subject.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `shows` by `show`.

observation: The proof says `we my apply Lemma ...`.
adverse_evidence: The modal verb is a typographical error.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `my` by `may`.

observation: After `Let $R$ be ... Let $K$ be ...`, the hypothesis reads `Let $R\subset K$ and $K$ is of finite type over $R$`.
adverse_evidence: The imperative `Let` cannot govern the coordinated finite clause `$K$ is ...`; this is a pair of assumptions about the already introduced objects.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `Assume $R\subset K$ and that $K$ is of finite type over $R$`.

observation: The lemma says `Write $f:Y\to X$ the induced map of spectra`.
adverse_evidence: In this construction `write [symbol] for [object]`, the preposition `for` is required between the notation and its referent.
proposed_smallest_correction: Insert `for`: `Write $f:Y\to X$ for the induced map of spectra`.

observation: The compound subject `This diagram and the density ...` is followed by the singular verb `shows`.
adverse_evidence: The diagram and the density are two coordinated grounds for the conclusion and take plural agreement.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `shows` by `show`.

observation: The proof begins `We saw, Lemma ... that ...`.
adverse_evidence: The cited lemma is the locus in which the result was seen; the construction requires the preposition `in`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Insert `in`: `We saw, in Lemma ..., that ...`.

observation: For $n\ge0$, the proof displays `0\to K_n\to F_{n-1}\to\cdots\to F_0\to M\to0` without separating $n=0$.
adverse_evidence: At $n=0$ the display invokes the undefined module $F_{-1}$. The local-projectivity argument still works by setting $K_0=M$, whose localizations are projective under the hypothesis.
proposed_smallest_correction: Handle $n=0$ explicitly by setting $K_0=M$; use the displayed syzygy resolution only for $n\ge1$.

observation: The proof says the maps `have to property that ...`.
adverse_evidence: The phrase contains a typographical substitution of `to` for the definite article.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `to` by `the`.

observation: With $d=\dim S\ge0$, the proof sets `$K_d=\ker(F_{d-1}\to F_{d-2})$` without separating $d=0,1$.
adverse_evidence: For $d=1$ the first syzygy is $\ker(F_0\to\kappa)$, while for $d=0$ it is $K_0=\kappa$; the printed formula otherwise invokes $F_{-1}$ or $F_{-2}$ and the following exact complex is not defined at the allowed boundary values.
proposed_smallest_correction: Define $K_0=\kappa$, $K_1=\ker(F_0\to\kappa)$, and $K_d=\ker(F_{d-1}\to F_{d-2})$ only for $d\ge2$; adapt the displayed complex accordingly.

observation: The introduction says `images of a constructible is constructible`.
adverse_evidence: The phrase omits the noun `set` after `constructible` and combines a plural subject with a singular verb.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `the image of a constructible set is constructible`.

observation: The notation paragraph says `Write $f:Y\to X$ the induced map of spectra`.
adverse_evidence: The construction `write [symbol] for [object]` requires the preposition `for`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Insert `for` after the displayed map.

observation: The lemma begins with the sentence fragment `With notation as above.` followed by `Assume ...`.
adverse_evidence: The initial prepositional phrase has no predicate and modifies the following assumption.
proposed_smallest_correction: Join the clauses: `With notation as above, assume that ...`.

observation: For $f:Y\to X$, the proof says `the image of a constructible set in $X$ is constructible in $Y$`.
adverse_evidence: Chevalley's theorem applies to a constructible subset of the source $Y$ and places its image in the target $X$; the printed sentence reverses source and target.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `in $X$ ... in $Y$` by `in $Y$ ... in $X$`.

observation: The proof says that if `$\mathfrak p$ is any ideal containing $xy$, then either $x$ or $y$` lies in it.
adverse_evidence: This implication is false for an arbitrary ideal: $(xy)$ contains $xy$ but contains neither $x$ nor $y$. It is precisely the prime-ideal property used by the next sentence about minimal primes; the sentence also describes element membership as containment.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `any ideal` by `any prime ideal` and say `either $x$ or $y$ belongs to $\mathfrak p$`.

observation: The polynomial ring ends `$k[\ldots,y_{22}])$` with a closing parenthesis for which no opening parenthesis exists.
adverse_evidence: The ring expression begins directly with `$k[` and should close only its square bracket before the math delimiter.
proposed_smallest_correction: Delete the unmatched `)` after the closing square bracket.

observation: The proof says `the image of irreducible an algebraic set`.
adverse_evidence: The indefinite article and adjectives are in the wrong order.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `the image of an irreducible algebraic set`.

observation: The parenthesis reads `reason($Y=0$ is contained the previous case)`.
adverse_evidence: A space is missing before the parenthesis, `contained` lacks the preposition `in`, and the intended relation is that the zero case was already covered rather than that an equation is a subset.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `reason (the case $Y=0$ was covered above):` or an equivalent idiomatic parenthesis.

observation: The example says `$T$ is classified by the its rank`.
adverse_evidence: Two determiners are duplicated before `rank`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Delete `the`: `classified by its rank`.

observation: The example says `every idempotent matrix is contained in one such orbit`.
adverse_evidence: A matrix is an element of an orbit, not a subset contained in it.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `belongs to one such orbit` (or `lies in`).

observation: The positive-characteristic example says `$char=3$` with an undefined bare symbol `char`.
adverse_evidence: The characteristic belongs to the base field $k$ introduced in the example.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `$\operatorname{char}(k)=3$` or `if $k$ has characteristic $3$`.

observation: In characteristic $3$, the example claims $\operatorname{tr}(\wedge^3T)$ is $1$ on the rank-$3$ component and $0$ on every other component.
adverse_evidence: For an idempotent of rank $r$, this trace is $\binom r3$ in $k$. Rank $4$ already gives $\binom43=4=1$ in characteristic $3$, so the stated separation is false whenever $n\ge4$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use the valid general separation: for ranks $r<s$, $\operatorname{tr}(\wedge^sT)$ is $0$ on rank $r$ and $1$ on rank $s$; or explicitly restrict the printed illustration to $n=3$.

observation: In the depth-zero base case, $e=\operatorname{pd}_R(M)$ may be $0$ or $1$, but the displayed decomposition simultaneously starts with $K_{e-2}$ and ends with $K_0$.
adverse_evidence: At $e=0$ or $e=1$ this invokes $K_{-2}$ or $K_{-1}$ and does not describe the minimal resolution. The desired depth inequality is immediate/direct in those two short cases; the printed chain is valid only for $e\ge2$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Treat $e=0$ and $e=1$ directly, then introduce the displayed chain and its $K_i$ only for $e\ge2$.

observation: The quasi-finite reduction says `an element $g'\in S'$ such that $g'\notin\mathfrak q$ such that ...`, where $\mathfrak q\subset S$.
adverse_evidence: The sentence duplicates `such that`, and an element of $S'$ cannot literally be tested for membership in an ideal of $S$ without applying the map $S'\to S$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `an element $g'\in S'$ whose image in $S$ does not belong to $\mathfrak q$ and such that ...`.

observation: Condition (b) reads `$S$ finite over $R$`.
adverse_evidence: The predicate adjective requires the copula, parallel to conditions (a), (c), and (d).
proposed_smallest_correction: Insert `is`: `$S$ is finite over $R$`.

observation: After defining the ideal $\overline I\subset\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x]$, the proof chooses its monic generator `$\overline h\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$`.
adverse_evidence: A nonconstant generator of an ideal in the polynomial PID belongs to $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x]$, not merely to its coefficient field.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the membership target by `$\overline h\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x]$`.

observation: The proof rescales the generator $\overline h$ by `some $\lambda\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$` without requiring $\lambda\ne0$.
adverse_evidence: Multiplication by zero destroys the generator and the subsequent factorization; rescaling a generator is valid only by a unit of the residue field.
proposed_smallest_correction: Require `$\lambda\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)^\times$` (or explicitly `$\lambda\ne0$`).

observation: The factorization defines only $e_2,\ldots,e_n$, then asserts `$A_i=\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x]/(\overline h_i^{e_i})$` without restricting $i$.
adverse_evidence: The exponent $e_1$ is undefined; the preceding factorization gives the separable factor $\overline h_1$ exponent one and identifies $A_1$ with its residue-field quotient.
proposed_smallest_correction: Set `$e_1=1$` explicitly before the uniform formula, or restrict the formula to $i\ge2$ and state $A_1=\kappa(\mathfrak p)[x]/(\overline h_1)$ separately.

observation: The conditional hypothesis ends `If $\mathfrak q\subset S$ is a maximal ideal.` and the next sentence begins `Then ...`.
adverse_evidence: The period separates the if-clause from its required main clause.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the period after `ideal` by a comma and continue `then ...`.

observation: With $e=\dim(R_{\mathfrak p})\ge0$, the going-down construction unconditionally starts by choosing $\mathfrak q_{-1}$ over $\mathfrak p_{e-1}$.
adverse_evidence: When $e=0$, $\mathfrak p_{-1}$ is undefined and the original fibre chain $\mathfrak q_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathfrak q_d$ already has the required length $d$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Separate the case $e=0$; run the negative-index going-down construction only for $e\ge1$.

observation: The hypothesis says `Assume $R$ Cohen-Macaulay`.
adverse_evidence: The predicate adjective requires the copula.
proposed_smallest_correction: Insert `is`: `Assume $R$ is Cohen-Macaulay`.

observation: For arbitrary maps $R_i\to S_i$, the lemma concludes that the maps `$R\to S$` and `$R_i\to S_i$` are `integrally closed`.
adverse_evidence: The immediately preceding definition defines only a subring $R\subset S$ as integrally closed in $S$; it does not define an arbitrary ring map as integrally closed, and the displayed maps were not assumed injective.
proposed_smallest_correction: Either add injectivity hypotheses and say `$R$ is integrally closed in $S$ iff each $R_i$ is integrally closed in $S_i$`, or explicitly define the intended map-level property before using it.

observation: The proof says `Let $S$ integral over $k$`.
adverse_evidence: The predicate adjective requires the copula.
proposed_smallest_correction: Insert `be`: `Let $S$ be integral over $k$`.

observation: To prove a finite-dimensional domain $S$ is a field, the proof says `Pick $s\in S$` and claims multiplication by $s$ is surjective.
adverse_evidence: Multiplication by $0$ is not surjective in a nonzero algebra; the dimension argument applies because multiplication by a nonzero element of a domain is injective.
proposed_smallest_correction: Require `Pick a nonzero $s\in S$`.

observation: The proof concludes `there are at most finitely many` primes.
adverse_evidence: The intended conclusion is simple finiteness; `at most finitely many` is redundant and non-idiomatic.
proposed_smallest_correction: Use `there are only finitely many`.

observation: For a retraction $\tau:R'\to R$, the proof writes `$\mathfrak m=\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m')$` with $\mathfrak m'\subset R'$.
adverse_evidence: Inverse image under $\tau$ takes an ideal of the codomain $R$ to one in the domain $R'$; the printed expression is ill-typed. The parallel proof at line 42250 gives the correct relation.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace it by `$\mathfrak m'=\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$`.

observation: The tensor-base-change product begins with the $A'_1$ factor and also ends its ellipsis with another `$A'_1\otimes_{R',\tau}R$`.
adverse_evidence: The preceding product has distinct factors $A'_1,\ldots,A'_n$, and the following line names their base changes $A_1,\ldots,A_n$; the final displayed factor must be the $n$th one.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the second `$A'_1$` by `$A'_n$`.

observation: The definition says that every almost integral element of the fraction field is `contained in $R$`.
adverse_evidence: An element belongs to a ring; it is not a subset contained in the ring.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `is contained in $R$` by `belongs to $R$`.

observation: The proof says `there exists an $d>0$`.
adverse_evidence: The indefinite article before the consonant sound of $d$ must be `a`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `an` by `a`.

observation: After defining $P=x^d+\sum_{j<d}a_jx^j$, the proof quantifies the same coefficients as $a_i$ in two consecutive sentences.
adverse_evidence: No independent index $i$ is introduced; the polynomial and the scaled polynomial both use the summation index $j$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace both coefficient occurrences `$a_i$` by `$a_j$`.

observation: The proof says `the set of almost integral elements form a subring`.
adverse_evidence: The grammatical subject is the singular noun `set`.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `form` by `forms`.

observation: For a finite etale $R$-algebra $S=\prod A_i$, the proof says each local factor $A_i$ is finite etale over $S$.
adverse_evidence: Each $A_i$ is a factor of $S$ and is finite etale over the base ring $R$; the following reduction modulo $\mathfrak m$ and cited henselian lemmas use the $R$-algebra structure.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `finite etale over $S$` by `finite etale over $R$`.

observation: For an $R$-algebra map $\varphi:S_1\to S_2$, the induced multiplication map on $S_1\otimes_RS_2$ is printed as `$\varphi\times1$`.
adverse_evidence: The map from the tensor product is induced by the tensor product of $\varphi$ with the identity followed by multiplication; the symbol $\times$ is not the tensor-product map used here.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace `$\varphi\times1$` by `$\varphi\otimes1$`.

observation: The set-builder expression is printed as `$I=\{f\in R, fx\in R\}$`.
adverse_evidence: The comma does not mark the predicate of the set-builder unambiguously; the standard TeX notation here is a vertical bar or colon.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace the comma after `$f\in R$` by `$\mid$` (or a colon).

observation: The proof says `Denote $e_i=(\ldots)$ the $i$th idempotent`.

observation: The proof says that elements `$a,b\in R$` `come from objects $a_i,b_i$ over $R_i$`.

observation: The conclusion names $R_{\mathfrak m}$ but quantifies every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$, including $\mathfrak p=(0)$.
adverse_evidence: The localization variable is inconsistent, and the DVR claim used in condition (2) concerns nonzero primes or maximal ideals.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a DVR for every nonzero prime $\mathfrak p$, or consistently use $R_{\mathfrak m}$ for every nonzero maximal $\mathfrak m$.

observation: The factorization argument starts with an arbitrary ideal $I$.
adverse_evidence: The zero ideal is outside the Dedekind factorization requirement, while $I=R$ is not prime and is contained in no maximal ideal, so the next selection of $\mathfrak p$ fails.
proposed_smallest_correction: Take $I$ nonzero; dispose of $I=R$ by the empty product, then assume $I$ is proper.

observation: Noetherian induction is invoked for $J=(I:\mathfrak p)$ without proving $J$ strictly contains $I$.
adverse_evidence: Strict containment is required to apply induction on larger ideals; $J\mathfrak p=I$ alone does not state it.
proposed_smallest_correction: At $\mathfrak p$, write $I_{\mathfrak p}=(\pi^n)$ with $n\ge1$ and observe $J_{\mathfrak p}=(\pi^{n-1})\supsetneq I_{\mathfrak p}$.

observation: The proof explicitly omits uniqueness of prime-ideal factorization.
adverse_evidence: Uniqueness is part of the definition of a Dedekind domain, so existence alone does not establish the implication to condition (1).
proposed_smallest_correction: Supply uniqueness by localizing both factorizations at each nonzero maximal ideal and comparing DVR valuation exponents.

observation: Both directions in the Nagata proof infer divisibility by $p_1\cdots p_r$ from the statement that each $p_i$ divides the same element.
adverse_evidence: If prime factors repeat, individual divisibility does not preserve multiplicity; for example $p$ divides $y$ does not imply $p^2$ divides $y$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Divide and cancel the prime factors successively, updating the remaining equality after each cancellation.

observation: The Dedekind definition quantifies every nonzero ideal but writes only a product of prime ideals without specifying the empty product.
adverse_evidence: The unit ideal $R$ is nonzero and cannot be a positive product of proper prime ideals.
proposed_smallest_correction: Allow $r=0$ explicitly and declare the empty product to be $R$.

observation: The proof applies the Dedekind characterization after establishing only Noetherianity and dimension one.
adverse_evidence: The cited characterization also requires normality; $B$ is normal because it is the integral closure and its fraction field is $L$, but that step is absent.
proposed_smallest_correction: Add that $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=L$ and that, as the integral closure of $A$ in $L$, $B$ is integrally closed and hence normal.

observation: The list of possible associates is printed as '$a_1,\ldots,b_m$'.
adverse_evidence: This omits the endpoint $a_n$ and merges two distinct factor lists, obscuring the dichotomy needed for $a\in(x)$ or $b\in(x)$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write '$a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_m$'.

observation: The quotient expressions are printed without grouping: $M/M \cap M'$, $M'/M \cap M'$, and $M + M' / M'$.
adverse_evidence: Under ordinary parsing these expressions are ill-typed and do not denote the quotient modules used by the proof or the distance definition.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write $M/(M\cap M')$, $M'/(M\cap M')$, $(M+M')/M'$, and $(M+M')/M$ at every occurrence.

observation: The left side $d(M, \varphi(\psi((M)))$ lacks the closing parenthesis for $d($ and contains redundant grouping around $M$.
adverse_evidence: The expression is syntactically unbalanced and cannot denote the distance used in the following equality chain.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write $d(M, \varphi(\psi(M)))$.

observation: The proof writes $E_1(a)(R^{\oplus b})$ although $b$ is undefined.
adverse_evidence: The ambient vector space has dimension $n$, and the same line and the next line use $R^{\oplus n}$ and $R^{\oplus n-1}$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace $R^{\oplus b}$ by $R^{\oplus n}$.

observation: The sentence says that $S_1'$ 'is Artinian ring'.
adverse_evidence: The singular count noun ring requires an article; the omission makes the source sentence ungrammatical.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write 'is an Artinian ring'.

observation: The proof invokes 'the stability of finite type property under base change'.
adverse_evidence: The bare noun phrase is ungrammatical and obscures that the property of being of finite type is meant.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write 'the stability under base change of the property of being of finite type'.

observation: After defining the family of monic polynomials $P_i$, the proof twice writes $P(x_i)^{e_i}=0$.
adverse_evidence: The symbol $P$ is undefined; local nilpotence applies separately to each already defined element $P_i(x_i)$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Replace both occurrences by $P_i(x_i)^{e_i}=0$.

observation: The lemma permits $n=0$, but its proof multiplies by $\varphi(a_n)^{n-1}$.
adverse_evidence: For $n=0$ this calls for exponent $-1$ even though the conclusion is immediate because $\varphi(a_0)=0$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Handle $n=0$ separately, or assume $n\geq1$ before the displayed multiplication.

observation: The proof says 'multiply the equation ... with $\varphi(a_n)^{n-1}$'.
adverse_evidence: Standard English for multiplication uses 'by' rather than 'with'.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write 'multiply the equation ... by $\varphi(a_n)^{n-1}$'.

observation: The situation says 'Assume $\varphi(R) \subset S$ integrally closed in $S$'.
adverse_evidence: The modifier is grammatically attached to the inclusion rather than clearly asserting the property of the subring $\varphi(R)$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write 'Assume that $\varphi(R)$ is integrally closed in $S$'.

observation: The lemma says 'Assume $x\in S$ be strongly transcendental over $R$'.
adverse_evidence: The construction 'Assume ... be' is ungrammatical in this declarative context.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write 'Assume $x\in S$ is strongly transcendental over $R$'.

observation: The proof says 'The base case is $m=0$ is vacuous'.
adverse_evidence: The duplicated finite verb makes the sentence ungrammatical.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write 'The base case $m=0$ is vacuous'.

observation: Both cases infer $b_mx\in S'$ directly from Lemma ref{lemma-make-integral-trivial}.
adverse_evidence: The cited lemma gives integrality over $S'$; membership in $S'$ additionally uses that $S'$ is integral over $R$, transitivity of integrality, and the definition of $S'$ as the integral closure of $R$ in $S$.
proposed_smallest_correction: State the transitivity step before concluding $b_mx\in S'$, in both cases.

observation: The theorem says 'Let $R\to S$ be a finite type $R$-algebra'.
adverse_evidence: A ring homomorphism is not itself an $R$-algebra; $S$ is the algebra, or the map is a homomorphism of finite type.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write 'Let $S$ be an $R$-algebra of finite type' or 'Let $R\to S$ be a ring homomorphism of finite type'.

observation: The proof says 'We prove the proposition by induction'.
adverse_evidence: The enclosing result is a theorem, not a proposition.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write 'We prove the theorem by induction'.

observation: The parenthesis says '(For example generators of $S$ over $R$.)'.
adverse_evidence: The fragment lacks a finite verb and the expected introductory comma.
proposed_smallest_correction: Write '(For example, take generators of $S$ over $R$.)'.

observation: The explanation consists of the fragments 'Surjectivity because ... injectivity because ...'.
adverse_evidence: Both clauses lack finite verbs, and the exactness argument belongs with injectivity.
proposed_smallest_correction: State that surjectivity follows from the choice of the $y_i$ and injectivity from $R''\subset R'$ together with exactness of localization.

observation: The quasi-finite extension lemma invokes $\operatorname{ord}_{B_{\mathfrak m_i}}$ for every maximal ideal and the proof treats $\mathfrak n_i=C\cap\mathfrak m_i$ as maximal under hypotheses that permit $B=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$.
adverse_evidence: For $A=k[t]_{(t)}$ and $B=k(t)=A[1/t]$, all stated hypotheses hold, but the unique maximal ideal is $(0)$; $B_{(0)}$ has dimension zero so Definition definition-ord does not apply, $[\kappa((0)):\kappa(\mathfrak m_A)]=[k(t):k]$ need not be finite, and $\mathfrak n_i=(0)$ is not maximal in the finite algebra $C$.
proposed_smallest_correction: Add the hypothesis that $B$ is not a field (equivalently here, $\dim(B)=1$ or $\mathfrak m_A B\ne B$), so every maximal ideal lies over $\mathfrak m_A$ and the local orders and proof recurrence are well-typed.
